implementation_status.note: Reuses Slither's OWN ERC20/ERC721 resemblance heuristics (Contract.is_possible_erc20/is_possible_erc721, which match against the ERC's own canonical required-signature list in slither/utils/erc.py) and Slither's OWN interface-correctness checkers (IncorrectERC20InterfaceDetection/IncorrectERC721InterfaceDetection) rather than re-deriving a signature list -- same analyzer-reuse discipline as L4/L5, applied to a GP requirement. Only covers ERC20/ERC721 (the two Slither ships interface checkers for); ERC1155/ERC4626/etc. resemblance detection is NOT implemented (Slither has no equivalent canonical signature list for them) and is left as an explicit gap rather than a hand-derived one. Evidence-only, deliberately: signature-shape resemblance + return-type correctness does not establish full ERC conformance (events, additional invariants) or whether pursuing the ERC was 'reasonably' applicable to the use-case -- both remain semantic judgments, not attempted here.
